title: Hubballi-Dharwad cotton ginning & pressing: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
A ginning and pressing unit buys seed cotton (kapas) at the mandi, separates lint from seed, bales and presses the lint, and sells to spinning mills; seed and cotton oil cake are by-products. **Cash is made on the spread between kapas cost and lint sale price, not on volume alone.** The ginning step adds little value, so the industry is fragmented with low entry barriers and competition is stiff [6]. Profitability is exposed to agro-climatic risk and to how much working capital is borrowed [8].

## Where value and cash sit now
Peer results show the split clearly: AB Cotspin's Q1 FY27 revenue rose 52.94% to Rs 102.01 crore while operating margin fell to 12.90% from 22.29% in the September 2025 quarter, so higher volume is earning thinner spreads [1][2]. Sportking India nearly doubled EBITDA margin to 19.8% in Q2 FY27 from 10.4% in Q2 FY26 on better realisations [4]. **The lesson for us: margin, not turnover, is the credit story.** Proximity to cotton-growing areas helps control logistics cost and supports margin [7].

## The local picture and the growth opening
Our sources say almost nothing about Hubballi-Dharwad itself, so lean on first principles and peers. The official data pack gives Karnataka GST collections +11.1% Apr-to-date against India +6.1%, and electricity demand +23.3% against India +9.5% [D]; India-wide cotton-linked output (NIC 13) is +13.1% YoY [D]. **Pursue ginners with captive pressing, a named mill buyer list and by-product income; avoid pure job-work units and traders.** When a proposal lands, check the buyer list and whether seed/cake sales are contracted; if the unit sells only to one or two mills, ask for the last twelve months of invoices.

## How to grow safely
Structure against stock, not against hope. Take monthly stock statements and insurance on kapas and lint, and set the drawing power on audited stock. **Take every month: stock and book-debt statements, a ginning yield report, and the sales register by buyer.** Where the unit is close to cotton areas, ask for the logistics cost line [7]. If the promoter's net worth is small and working capital is fully borrowed, size the limit to the by-product cash flow [8].

## Early-warning signs
Watch margin compression first: a fall like AB Cotspin's 22.29% to 12.90% means volume is being bought with price [1][2]. **Trigger: two quarters of falling margin with rising turnover -> cut limit and ask for buyer contracts.** Also watch stretched capital structure and high reliance on external borrowings [8], and any single-buyer concentration above the stated book [7]. Collect from customer the local kapas arrival and price data; we do not have it.
watch: Stock cover falls below drawing power for two months -> freeze further drawing and inspect godown
Operating margin falls two quarters running -> reduce limit and seek buyer contracts
Top buyer exceeds half of sales -> ask for diversification plan and additional collateral
Seed/cake realisation drops sharply -> rework drawing power on revised cash flow
